newsitem.title: USA: Semiconductor market to rise 12.1 percent - Dataquest.
newsitem.headline: Semiconductor market to rise 12.1 percent - Dataquest.

text.p: The worldwide market for computer chips likely will rise 12.1 percent to $158.7 billion in 1997, reflecting higher chip prices and strong demand, market researcher Dataquest said Wednesday.

Worldwide revenue for memory chips -- the electronic components that store information for the computer to process -- will drop about 5 percent to $24.6 billion, said Jim Handy, director of Dataquest's semiconductor research.
But sales of microprocessors -- the chips that do the number-cruching in a computer -- will rise 28 percent to $23.9 billion, offsetting the memory chip drop.
Dataquest estimated the compound annual growth rate for the industry will be 17.6 percent from 1996 through 2001, with revenue reaching $318.2 billion in 2001.

The researcher also said the market for digital signal processors -- the electronics that convert real-world information, such as sound and temperature, into digital computer information -- could grow about 30 percent during each year in 1997 and 1998, reaching $4 billion by 1998.
